overall_comment: The imaging features for this 48-year-old patient are highly suggestive of a high-grade glioma. The right temporal lobe mass demonstrates a large non-enhancing component but also contains definite areas of necrosis and thick-margin enhancement. The presence of necrosis is the strongest indicator for a WHO Grade 4 tumor. This feature, combined with the patient's age and deep gray matter involvement, strongly favors an IDH-wildtype status. The temporal location makes a 1p/19q co-deletion highly unlikely. All findings converge on a consistent diagnosis of Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype.
